ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, wedge A is placed at rest on the horizontal ground, wooden stake B is fixed on the horizontal ground, and spring K connects the object with the wooden stake; the spring is parallel to the inclined plane. The object of mass m and the person move downward along the surface of the wedge under the action of spring K; at this time the direction of the friction force exerted by the ground on the wedge is to the left. Then which of the following statements is correct ( )
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: If the spring is cut, the acceleration direction of the object and the person must be downward along the inclined plane

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, wedge A is placed on the horizontal ground, and the inclined plane rises from the lower left to the upper right; there is a fixed wooden stake B on the left side. One end of spring K is connected near the wooden stake, and the other end is connected to the block on the inclined plane; the direction of the spring is parallel to the inclined plane. Block m is on the inclined plane, and the position of the person in the figure is above the block; the direction downward along the inclined plane is toward the lower left, and the direction upward along the inclined plane is toward the upper right. Then reason: The stem states that the object and the person are moving downward along the surface of the wedge, so the friction force of the inclined plane on the object should be upward along the inclined plane. By action and reaction, the friction force of the object on the wedge is downward along the inclined plane, and its horizontal component is to the left; the normal pressure of the object on the wedge is perpendicular to the inclined plane and points into the interior of the wedge, and its horizontal component is to the right. The stem also gives that the direction of the friction force exerted by the ground on the wedge is to the left, and the wedge is at rest, which shows that the horizontal resultant force of the object on the wedge must be to the right, in order to be balanced by the leftward friction force from the ground. Thus the rightward component of the normal pressure of the object on the wedge is greater than the leftward component of the friction force, namely N sinθ > f cosθ. Since the spring is parallel to the inclined plane, the spring force has no component perpendicular to the inclined plane, so in the direction perpendicular to the inclined plane the object still has N = mg cosθ. Substituting into N sinθ > f cosθ gives mg sinθ > f, that is, the component of gravity downward along the inclined plane is greater than the magnitude of the friction force upward along the inclined plane. After the spring is cut, only the spring force along the inclined-plane direction is removed; the force relation in the direction perpendicular to the inclined plane is unchanged, and the friction force still points upward to hinder its sliding downward. Since mg sinθ is still greater than the friction force f, the resultant force along the inclined-plane direction is still downward, so the acceleration of the object and the person must be downward along the inclined plane.
